Tamil Cinema’s dream of 1000 crore box office still remains unfulfilled

Kollywood has experienced massive blockbuster successes over the years, but the elusive one thousand crore club remains unconquered. Industry analysts note that while several Tamil films have crossed major milestones globally, none have officially touched this massive financial figure yet. Big-budget action thrillers and star-driven projects frequently generate record-breaking collections worldwide upon release. However, consistent overseas performance and unprecedented domestic theatrical runs are required to push a Tamil film past this ultimate threshold. Fans and trade experts continue to debate which upcoming big-scale franchise might finally break this barrier. This milestone remains the most anticipated achievement for the Tamil film industry in the near future.

5e87819159.caption:
Renowned cinematographer Shaji Kumar passed away in the early hours of November 10 at a private hospital in Kochi. He was 57. He was taken ill on November 7 while shooting a Dileep film in Alappuzha and was moved to Kochi, where he died of cardiac failure.

Shaji Kumar began his career as an independent cinematographer with Uthaman in 2001 and went on to shoot some of Malayalam cinema's biggest films, including Pulimurugan, Naran, Odiyan, Pokkiri Raja, Ramaleela, Pathonpatham Noottandu and Thudarum. In Tamil, he worked on Ponnar Shankar, Mambattiyan and Saahasam. His last works include Mohanlal's Athimanoharam, directed by Tharun Moorthy.

Rest in peace, Shaji Kumar. Thank you for the visuals that made us fall in love with cinema.
